## Why this demo exists

::: {.callout-why-this-matters}
Lecture 9 is where students learn that spectra are not just “pretty rainbows.” Spectral lines are **measurable features** that encode composition — and they are only useful if students can recognize **patterns**, not just memorize a single line.
:::

This demo is built around your course loop:

- **Predict:** which setup produces continuous vs emission vs absorption?
- **Play:** add and remove element cards; broaden the instrument; overlay an unknown.
- **Explain:** commit to an element set and check the match.

## Learning goals (ASTR 101)

Students should be able to:

1. Predict which spectrum type appears for a physical setup (continuous / emission / absorption).
2. Explain why absorption and emission occur at the **same wavelengths** (inverted contrast).
3. Identify an unknown spectrum by matching **line patterns** to element cards.

## 10–15 minute live-teach script (projector)

1. Open the student demo: `/demos/spectral-lines-lab/`
2. **Mission A (Kirchhoff):** Ask: “Which setup produces absorption lines?” Then click through setups and narrate what changes physically.
3. **Fingerprint idea:** Multi-select Hydrogen and Sodium. Ask: “If I add a second element, what happens to the spectrum?” (Prediction first, then reveal.)
4. Turn on the unknown overlay. Ask students to vote on which element(s) are present and why (pattern matching).
5. **Key takeaway sentence:** “Astronomers identify elements by **patterns of features** at specific wavelengths, not by one magic line.”

## Misconceptions to target (quick prompts)

- “Elements have one signature line.” → Ask: “Would two different elements ever share one line by coincidence?”
- “Absorption and emission lines happen at different wavelengths.” → Ask: “If it’s the same transition, should the photon energy change?”

## Connections to other demos

- **Blackbody radiation:** provides the continuous background that absorption lines sit on.
- **Doppler Shift Spectrometer:** the same line pattern shifts together when the source moves.
- **Binary orbits (RV overlay):** tracking the shifting line over time builds the RV curve.
